basics.name: Alan Karp
basics.label: AI Program Manager
basics.summary: Manufacturing and process engineer turned AI operations leader. Since 2017: process engineering, plant operations and enterprise transformation in PE-backed manufacturing. At DwyerOmega, led AI and enterprise transformation across 6 acquisitions ($800M+), consolidating 27 enterprise systems and reporting to the CIO. Now founder of Syrup Labs AI, where I apply measurement-system, process-control and lean thinking to AI: every agent output is checked by something that can say no, and the checkers are themselves checked. MBA, Villanova (Strategic Management, Analytics, AI/ML). B.S. Chemical Engineering, UMBC.

work.name: Syrup Labs AI (syrp.ai)
work.summary: Title of record: AI Automation Consultant. Pre-revenue AI enablement company, targeting three paying clients. Ran AI like a production line, with inspection built in.
highlights: Process control for AI work. Operate Mission Control, an open-source agent operations platform I extended: 100+ API routes, an agent task board with column gates, a decision ledger of 4,400+ recorded entries (1,000+ of them logged as failures), and quality gates that refuse to let work close without proof. Maintained across a 1,365-commit codebase.

Measurement systems. Built a golden-question exam that grades AI models and passes one only if the Wilson 95% lower bound of its score clears the bar. Six local models graded; one passed (gemma4, 0.994 score, 0.965 lower bound over 20 runs), five failed.

Gauge discipline. Found that an internal research-grading judge returned a passing template and truncated 36% of its input, and closed that pipeline rather than ship it. Later fixed six checkers that reported success while testing nothing.
Independent verification. Built a signed-contract task executor in which a second model performs the acceptance check and writes a receipt (4 receipts, 3 passed).

Lean applied to AI operations. Mapped kanban and WIP limits, andon escalation, poka-yoke guards (build, secret and worktree guards), 5S and hoshin planning onto the agent fleet; a 5S census of 575 project folders flagged 351 as stale.

Reliability. Run a self-hosted stack of 5 containerized services continuously since June 2026 at $26 per month. Verified disaster recovery for 841 GB: encrypted backup with SHA-256 check, two verified snapshots and a completed cold restore.

Fleet and cost. Moved the coordinator and an assistant agent to a local model on a single-GPU workstation, cutting per-token cost for routine work. Track 9 active product lines with market research in IdeaBrowser.

Implemented low-code automation (GoHighLevel, HubSpot, n8n, Google Sheets, Gmail), eliminating 10+ hours of manual admin per week per deployment. Scoped a four-week, $15K fixed-price pilot proposal for a prospective client.

work.name: DwyerOmega
work.summary: Title of record: AI & Enterprise Transformation Manager. PE-backed industrial manufacturer; enterprise transformation spanning ERP/MRP, AMS, CRM/MarTech, and enterprise BI.
highlights: Led AI and enterprise transformation across 6 acquisitions ($800M+), integrating ERP/MRP (SAP S/4HANA, SyteLine, QAD) and consolidating 27 enterprise systems.
Reported to the CIO and presented AI and transformation recommendations directly to PE stakeholders and C-suite leadership.
Built a knowledge base over historical ticket data that cut lookup time from 40 minutes to under 4 seconds.
Led the global rollout of one ticketing system spanning IT, EHS, facilities and manufacturing; retrained users to drive adoption after launch.
Owned the DO52 report, the company-wide dashboard used across DwyerOmega.
Served as Global Admin for Jira and Confluence; oversaw a 15-20 resource offshore vendor team.
Led greenfield implementation planning for enterprise AMS and Microsoft Fabric, coordinating cross-functional discovery with an external consulting partner.
Personally scoped and owned projects under a $1M threshold end to end; attended core engineering and stakeholder meetings on larger programs.
